boards.title: Only Happens Here: 10 Traditions That Make No Sense Anywhere Else
boards.description: Ten documented K-State rituals linking game days, graduation, campus landmarks and Wildcat identity across generations.

cards.title: Bend, Clap and Twist to Wabash
cards.subtitle: The synchronized movement born from K-State band history
cards.notes: Stand when the band starts, then follow the crowd’s established sequence of clapping, bending and twisting without blocking nearby seats.
cards.short_summary: A surviving piece of sheet music became the soundtrack for K-State’s most recognizable crowd movement.
cards.evidence_claim: K-State says the Wabash Cannonball became a tradition after the 1968 Nichols Hall fire and that fans now clap, bend and twist in synchronized motions when it is played.
cards.access_notes: Experience it when the song is performed at an open K-State event; event admission rules may apply.

cards.title: Sway Through the Alma Mater
cards.subtitle: A side-to-side ritual accompanying K-State’s 1888 song
cards.notes: Join the gentle side-to-side sway as the Alma Mater plays, keeping movements compact and following the pace set by those around you.
cards.short_summary: K-Staters turn their oldest university song into a shared physical expression of loyalty.
cards.evidence_claim: K-State documents that students, alumni and fans sway back and forth while singing the Alma Mater, written in 1888 and selected through a 1903 campus contest.
cards.access_notes: Participate whenever the Alma Mater is performed at an event open to you.

cards.title: Finish the Fight Song With Fists Up
cards.subtitle: The final gesture in K-State’s official fight song
cards.notes: Clap with “Wildcat Victory,” then watch for the closing line and raise your fists with the crowd rather than anticipating the cue.
cards.short_summary: The official fight song ends with a compact gesture that rewards knowing exactly when the final line arrives.
cards.evidence_claim: K-State identifies the 1927 composition “Wildcat Victory” as its official fight song and instructs participants to clap and pump their fists along with the final line.
cards.access_notes: Join during public performances; attendance requirements depend on the hosting event.

cards.title: Wear the One Official Color
cards.subtitle: Royal purple has stood alone since 1896
cards.notes: Choose a royal-purple layer for a campus day or public event; white, silver or black may accompany it, but purple carries the tradition.
cards.short_summary: Unlike schools with a paired palette, K-State has maintained one official university color since the nineteenth century.
cards.evidence_claim: K-State states that royal purple has remained the university’s only official color since 1896 and that faculty, staff and students regularly wear it.
cards.access_notes: This wearable tradition can be practiced anywhere; follow venue dress and safety requirements.

cards.title: Spell K-S-U With Three People
cards.subtitle: A Willie-inspired photo format shared by Wildcats
cards.notes: Gather three willing participants, assign one letter pose to each person and frame all three bodies clearly against a permitted backdrop.
cards.short_summary: A 2007 tailgate photo prompt grew into a recurring three-person pose printed in the alumni magazine.
cards.evidence_claim: The K-State Alumni Association traces the K-S-U photo tradition to the 2007 football season, when tailgaters were taught to pose like Willie after touchdowns; submissions began appearing in 2008.
cards.source_title: How the now-iconic K-S-U photo got its start
cards.access_notes: Pose only where photography and standing access are permitted; obtain consent from everyone pictured.

cards.title: Let Willie Keep the Mask On
cards.subtitle: The performer’s name remains a closely guarded K-State secret
cards.notes: Photograph and greet Willie as the mascot, and avoid pressing performers or staff to reveal who is inside the Wildcat head.
cards.short_summary: K-State preserves the character by keeping the student performer anonymous across public appearances.
cards.evidence_claim: The K-State Alumni Association says the identity of the people portraying Willie the Wildcat is a closely guarded secret and that the secrecy tradition has lasted more than 50 years.
cards.source_title: Willie the Wildcat (cont.) | K-State Alumni Association
cards.access_notes: Willie appears at selected university and community events; respect event boundaries and performer privacy.

cards.title: Count Willie’s Post-Touchdown Pushups
cards.subtitle: A mascot ritual performed after Wildcat scores
cards.notes: Watch from your assigned area and count along after a touchdown; leave the physical routine to Willie and keep aisles unobstructed.
cards.short_summary: Wildcat touchdowns cue a mascot exercise ritual that the crowd can follow without leaving its seats.
cards.evidence_claim: The K-State Alumni Association documents post-touchdown pushups as one of Willie the Wildcat’s game-day traditions.
cards.source_title: Top 5 reasons we think Willie the Wildcat is the best mascot
cards.access_notes: Visible during applicable football games; a valid event ticket and current stadium policies may apply.

cards.title: Refresh the Concrete K and S
cards.subtitle: Engineering students have maintained the hillside letters for generations
cards.notes: Learn the history from the roadside or join only through the authorized Tau Beta Pi service project; do not enter the hillside independently.
cards.short_summary: Annual brush clearing, litter pickup and whitewashing keep Manhattan’s K and S letters visible.
cards.evidence_claim: K-State Engineering reports that Tau Beta Pi members have cleared brush, collected trash and whitewashed K-Hill’s concrete K and S each fall since 1974.
cards.source_title: K-Hill History | Carl R. Ice College of Engineering
cards.access_notes: Hillside maintenance is an organized service activity; participate only with authorization and supervision.

cards.title: Receive the Ring in a Spring Ceremony
cards.subtitle: A formal handoff for qualified K-State ring recipients
cards.notes: If eligible and ordering a ring, confirm the current ceremony process with the Alumni Association well before the spring presentation.
cards.short_summary: K-State’s ring program culminates in an annual ceremony for new recipients rather than a simple retail pickup.
cards.evidence_claim: The K-State Alumni Association states that it sponsors a ceremony each spring for new recipients of the Official K-State Ring.
cards.source_title: The Official K-State Ring | K-State Alumni Association
cards.access_notes: Participation is limited to eligible ring recipients and governed by the Alumni Association’s current arrangements.

cards.title: Frame the Cap and Gown at the Gate
cards.subtitle: A commencement-season portrait at K-State’s limestone entrance
cards.notes: Bring academic regalia, use the public approach without blocking pedestrians and take turns composing the gate behind the graduate.
cards.short_summary: Graduates mark their transition from student to alum with a portrait at the campus’s wrought-iron gateway.
cards.evidence_claim: K-State documents taking a cap-and-gown photograph at Higinbotham Gate as a university tradition and notes the gate as a common graduation portrait setting.
cards.access_notes: Use the gate from publicly accessible campus walkways and yield to pedestrians and scheduled activities.
